voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, True - Crime & Horror Narrator (tZssYepgGaQmegsMEXjK), one take split into lines, inner pauses cut to 0.35 s, atempo 1.03

lines.text: If a wall in your house looks like this on a thermal camera, don't knock.
lines.beat_before: hook: the thermal camera on the blank wall, a warm rectangle

lines.text: I inspect houses. The camera shows me what walls are hiding. Leaks. Wiring. Mice.
lines.beat_before: the van at the empty house; the camera in a gloved hand

lines.text: Last month, a house that had been empty for a year. Power off. Heating off. Cold as a fridge.
Upstairs, the hallway ends in a blank wall. On the plans, there's nothing behind it.
lines.beat_before: the stairs; the hallway; the blank wall

lines.text: On my camera, there's a warm rectangle. Room sized. Thirty seven degrees.
Outside, I measure. Two metres of house you can't reach from inside.
lines.beat_before: outside: the tape measure along the side wall
back at the wall, the hand raised
three knocks; silence; two knocks answer through the wall

lines.text: I write it up as possible water damage. I don't tell the buyers.
lines.beat_before: stinger in silence; the van pulling away

lines.text: They moved in on Friday. This morning, they sent me a photo.
They want to know why the wall is warm to the touch.
And why there's a door in it now.
lines.beat_before: the photo: a door in the wall
